R06.definition_control: Rectangles were set from the pooled, label-blind anchor ranges and the observed adjective/amod band, before inspecting the adverb/depth responses in these windows. Expose adverb/advmod jointly, LY marker area and a separate three-axis depth view. No claim of exact matching or equal anchor distributions.
R06.title: Modifier bands with a depth response
R06.interaction: Inside fixed adjective/amod regions, the adverb/advmod band is often shared by Human and AI. Unfolding dependency depth reveals a lower AI layer in articles and parts of abstracts, while review AI occupies thin knots or strands rather than the broad Human depth spread. The common 15–25-token sentence-length companion retains these shapes. This changes the lead from a general high-adjective/low-adverb shift to a band with a collective depth response.
R06.exceptions: Email has substantial overlap and legal shares much of the length/depth geometry. The upper adjective regions often lack one class. Papers have only 23 documents per class and no Human points inside the selected common-length windows. The interval is not exact matching, and lower depth could still contribute mostly as a marginal or sentence-construction effect.
R06.capture_requirements: Retain which adjective region is occupied, the position and thickness of the adverb/advmod band, and the depth layer or knots above it. Allow branches, depth spread and genre variants; do not force one sign for adverb use. LY remains context, with no demonstrated necessary contribution. Sentence-length and source/segmentation context must remain visible.

genres.email: The lower adjective region contains a shared sloping adverb/advmod band. In the middle region AI also occupies an upper advmod branch at modest adverb values. Depth overlaps strongly; Human has some higher-depth points. The 15–25-token companion retains overlap. The upper region is effectively one-class support, so it cannot establish a class difference.
genres.review: Within lower and middle adjective regions, AI follows thin adverb/advmod branches and compact depth knots; Human extends around them with a much broader depth spread. In the length-context view AI forms narrow rising/turning strands around roughly similar short sentence lengths. Those knots persist in the common 15–25-token interval. The high-adverb direction is a variant of the earlier allocation hypothesis, not its disappearance.
genres.legal: Lower and middle regions show strongly shared adverb/advmod and sentence-length/depth scaffolds, with more Human high-depth and high-adverb extension. AI often fills lower parts of the depth cloud but overlaps extensively, including the common-length companion. The upper adjective region has very few Human points. Retain as a weak or partial variant rather than a clean depth-layer separation.
genres.abstracts: The middle and upper adjective regions show AI concentrated on lower-depth portions of the modifier configuration. The full length-context view also reveals shorter AI sentences. The common 15–25-token companion retains a lower AI depth layer with overlap, especially in the upper region with 28 Human and 27 AI representatives. The lower region is too sparse for a comparison.
genres.articles: The lower and middle adjective regions contain closely overlapping adverb/advmod bands. Depth separates their occupied layers much more clearly than the flat response projection: AI is mostly lower while Human extends above it. The length-context graphs show substantial sentence-length differences, but lower AI depth remains visible inside the 15–25-token interval (lower region 162 Human / 51 AI; middle 69 / 41). This is the strongest local example of a third response above a shared modifier band. Exact four-coordinate or exact-length matching has not been done.
genres.papers: Only the upper adjective region has meaningful two-class occupancy before length restriction, and it contains just 5 Human / 8 AI representatives with overlap and a lower AI tail. The 15–25-token companion has no Human points and only two AI points. No cross-class depth-layer conclusion is supported by that companion.

R04.definition_control: The earlier broad windows left different mean/median occupancy inside each region. These fixed raw-token rectangles are smaller companions, chosen before viewing their response slices. Apply identically to every genre and class; show empty/sparse cells and remaining anchor variation.
R04.title: Sentence spread and tail containment in narrower central bands
R04.interaction: After narrowing mean/median rectangles, the joint IQR/maximum response retains a thin low AI ribbon in short reviews and a lower AI envelope in short articles. Middle email and abstract regions show partial tail containment with substantial overlap. The minimum length remains marker context. This is a recurring response-envelope lead, not uniformly smaller AI variability.
R04.exceptions: Short email overlaps heavily. Legal overlaps through all three central regions and has long-tail AI points. Review middle/long windows and several article/abstract long windows lack AI support. Papers are too sparse. Remaining anchor variation and sentence counts have not been exactly controlled.
R04.capture_requirements: Represent the response envelope of IQR and maximum jointly around the mean/median region, including thin levels, Human fans, overlap and long-tail exceptions. Keep empty support visible. Do not replace the graph by a single global subtraction or maximum threshold.

genres.email: In the short narrow rectangle (69 Human / 243 AI), the IQR/maximum clouds substantially overlap. In the middle rectangle (16 / 84), Human includes higher maximum-length extension while AI has its own high-tail exceptions and broad overlap. The long rectangle has no AI points. A universal email containment statement is unsupported.
genres.review: The shared short rectangle (114 / 296) retains thin AI levels at low maximum length while IQR changes; Human fans into higher maxima. This is a clear local joint-response shape. The middle and long rectangles have no AI representatives, so they show occupancy differences rather than response comparisons.
genres.legal: The short, middle and long rectangles all contain both classes. Their IQR/maximum clouds overlap strongly and share a rising envelope, with Human upper-tail extension and some long-tail AI points. Legal is a material exception to a uniformly narrow low AI response.
genres.abstracts: The short rectangle is imbalanced (16 / 216) and overlaps considerably. In the middle rectangle (82 / 36), AI mainly occupies the lower IQR/maximum portion while Human extends upward and outward, with many shared points. The long rectangle has only one AI point and cannot establish a stable response shape.
genres.articles: The shared short rectangle (77 / 124) shows Human extending into a much higher joint IQR/maximum fan while AI occupies a lower envelope; there is overlap. The middle rectangle has only seven AI representatives and the long rectangle none. The short-region shape is the useful comparison here.
genres.papers: The short rectangle is empty, the middle contains only one AI point, and the long contains 2 Human / 8 AI. Their sparse spread is descriptive and does not establish recurring tail containment.

R05.definition_control: Maximum phrase frequencies use alphabetic word count. Integer rays occur in both classes. Recovered counts check CSV/extractor redundancies; raw-text counts were not independently verified.
R05.title: POS response along the same repetition branches
R05.interaction: Integer repeat maxima explain the visible normalized-frequency rays in both classes. After exposing recovered alphabetic word count and keeping the same maximum-bigram/maximum-trigram states, the POS-entropy response still differs in useful regions, especially legal and abstracts, and the (3,2) state in reviews and articles. Review AI also shows a genre-specific type-count plateau as word count increases. The branch identity itself is a measurement scaffold, not a discovery of AI-only rays.
R05.exceptions: Email branch responses overlap substantially; review (2,1) overlaps around the rising Human curve and (3,1) has only nine AI representatives. Article (2,1) and (3,1) have very few Human representatives. Papers occupy none of the three frozen low-repeat states. Word counts are visible, not exactly matched, and the audit recovers counts from CSV redundancies rather than independently reading raw texts.
R05.capture_requirements: Keep branch state, word-count position and POS response together. Preserve type-count saturation as a review-specific shape and avoid claiming it survives every genre. A future descriptor may follow a branch-dependent response curve with exceptions; no such descriptor was fitted in this pass.

genres.email: At the same repeat states the POS response rises with word count in both classes and overlaps heavily. AI often occupies a narrower lower portion, while Human has both higher and low-entropy exceptions. This is a weak conditional variant, not a clean class split.
genres.review: AI bigram/trigram type counts level off while total words increase; its POS response also remains in a narrow band. Within (2,1), AI overlaps the Human rising curve. Within (3,2), AI remains flatter and lower as Human extends upward with length. The (3,1) comparison is sparse on the AI side. These are specific response/branch shapes, not only smaller clouds.
genres.legal: Within (2,1), (3,1) and (3,2), useful overlapping word-count regions retain a lower AI POS-entropy cloud with overlap. The (2,1) state is best supported (76 Human / 179 AI). Both classes share the type-count/word-count scaffold. This retains the response lead after exposing the integer repetition explanation.
genres.abstracts: Within (2,1), AI occupies a lower POS-entropy layer across overlapping word counts (75 Human / 301 AI). The other states show a related lower AI response but have fewer AI points in (3,2). The type-count/length scaffold is shared. Remaining within-state count distributions are not identical.
genres.articles: Most Human and AI documents occupy different length/repetition regions. The (3,2) state provides a useful overlapping-count comparison (42 Human / 16 AI) with lower AI POS response. The (2,1) and (3,1) states have only 12 and 5 Human representatives, respectively, so the full-cloud difference cannot be treated as equally supported in every branch.
genres.papers: Full-count views show lower AI POS entropy over overlapping word-count ranges, but all three frozen repeat states are empty for both classes. The branch-conditioned finding is therefore unresolved for papers; the marginal full-context appearance cannot substitute for a missing branch comparison.

verbal_morphology.definition_control: Suffix matches are spelling patterns, not exact verb inflections. Verb diversity is bounded and can pile up at one. Auxiliary proportion and per-sentence passive-subject count have different denominators.
verbal_morphology.title: Suffix-conditioned lemma and auxiliary geometry
verbal_morphology.interaction: Inside the same ING/ED suffix rectangles, email, abstracts and articles tend to place AI toward high verb-lemma diversity with low auxiliary ratio, including vertical ceiling bands. Human occupies a broader lower-diversity/higher-auxiliary region. Reviews instead display several thin auxiliary strands across a large lemma-diversity range; legal overlaps or reverses the low-auxiliary direction. This is a recurring configuration with two major primary-genre variants, not a universal high-lemma/low-auxiliary rule.
verbal_morphology.exceptions: Legal does not support uniformly low AI auxiliaries, reviews reverse the lemma-variety direction in important branches, and papers do not reproduce the high-variety ceiling. Lemma ceilings can follow low verb count or short documents. The suffix regions do not exactly match length or verb count. Passive ratio and depth have not shown a necessary additional role.
verbal_morphology.capture_requirements: Keep the suffix-region context, bounded lemma ceiling, auxiliary response and review-specific thin strands. Inspect verb count and word/sentence-length support before designing a formula. Retain passive/depth as context until a recurring contribution is demonstrated.

genres.email: In the lower-ED region (105 Human / 190 AI), AI is mostly high in lemma variety and low in auxiliaries with a clear ceiling at one; Human spreads toward lower variety and higher auxiliaries. The higher-ED region has only 16 / 17 and overlaps more. The joint direction is useful locally but may depend on length or verb count.
genres.review: AI forms several near-horizontal auxiliary strands while lemma variety ranges widely, including much lower values than Human. Human is broader and often accumulates at the lemma ceiling. The two suffix regions both retain these thin AI structures. This is a strong local pattern and a directional exception to the high-variety AI configuration of email, abstracts and articles.
genres.legal: Human and AI overlap strongly in lemma variety, with a ceiling in both. AI often extends to higher auxiliary ratios within the same suffix regions, especially the higher-ED region. This contradicts a universal low-auxiliary AI direction; it remains a genre variant rather than evidence for the three-genre direction.
genres.abstracts: Both shared suffix regions show AI at high lemma variety and low auxiliary ratio relative to the broader Human response. The higher-ED region has 55 Human / 194 AI, with many AI points on the lemma ceiling and a low auxiliary strip. The lower-ED region is also supported (148 / 35). Ceiling and document-length explanations remain open.
genres.articles: The lower-ED region (308 / 290) shows a broad Human lemma/auxiliary cloud and an AI lower-right patch; the higher-ED region (107 / 43) retains the low-auxiliary/high-variety configuration with overlap. This is the best supported local suffix-conditioned example. A distinct six-member mechanism has not been established.
genres.papers: The lower-ED region contains only 16 Human / 11 AI and shows broad overlap with no AI ceiling at one; higher ED has only 3 / 1. Papers do not support the high-variety configuration and remain descriptive.

reference_organisation.definition_control: First/second-person word-list counts overlap total POS pronouns but are not identical tag sets. Sentence openings use a sentence denominator; word ratios use alphabetic words. Deixis is lexical-list based. Genre and source conventions can explain much of the pattern.
reference_organisation.title: Reference and sentence-opening organisation
reference_organisation.interaction: Total pronouns, pronoun sentence openings, person reference, deixis and nominal allocation show local mixtures and shared bands. The most visible differences change with genre and do not yet define one recurring collective configuration.
reference_organisation.exceptions: Abstract AI often has no pronoun openings or first-person use, whereas other genres have different person-reference branches. The relation may largely reflect source and genre conventions.

genres.email: AI occupies a narrow pronoun/opening region and a thin rising first-person branch; Human is broader along much of the same general relation. This alone is insufficient for a new interaction claim.
genres.review: AI shows disconnected pronoun/opening clusters and first-person branches; Human occupies a broader and more continuous arrangement with zero-axis cases. This is a local mixture, not a common cross-genre branch rule.
genres.legal: Total pronouns are low in both classes, openings are quantized and first-person zeros are frequent. AI has a rising first-person branch but shares substantial geometry with Human.
genres.abstracts: AI pronoun openings and first-person use are mostly zero, while Human varies considerably. This is a strong genre/source convention candidate rather than a recurring multi-genre signature.
genres.articles: Full pronoun/opening clouds overlap and first-person use has shared rising regions with broader Human extension. No clean new collective invariant was visible.
genres.papers: The sparse person-reference configurations do not reproduce the abstract zero pattern consistently. Record the difference without generalizing it.

discourse_clause_opening.definition_control: Discourse markers use case-insensitive substring counts per sentence, conjunctions use POS counts per alphabetic word, clause proxies overlap ccomp tokens and use sentence denominators. Opening stopwords use spaCy STOP.
discourse_clause_opening.title: Discourse, clauses and opening allocation
discourse_clause_opening.interaction: Marker/conjunction allocation and clause/length/opening responses show local branches, but their direction and occupied ranges vary by genre. Much of the apparent contrast reiterates the earlier clause/length lead or differences in overall support.
discourse_clause_opening.exceptions: Clause proxies share ccomp tokens and discourse markers are substring counts. A new stable surface is not established by the current projections.

genres.email: Low marker use is shared; AI has a compact higher-conjunction region with low clauses and considerable overlap. A distinct response band is unclear.
genres.review: AI has local conjunction/marker branches with different clause allocation, while Human fans more broadly. The shape is local and not repeated uniformly in other genres.
genres.legal: Marker-zero axes and low clause regions are common in both classes, with extensive overlap. No new recurring response surface is apparent.
genres.abstracts: AI occupies higher conjunction ranges with lower clause/opening profiles in parts of the graph, but occupancy shifts dominate the view.
genres.articles: AI is concentrated in lower conjunction and clause ranges near low markers; Human is broader. This may extend prior sentence/syntax findings rather than identify a separate mechanism.
genres.papers: Sparse configurations share much of the six-axis profile shape. No new stable interaction can be inferred.

lexical_frequency_information.definition_control: avg_freq_rank_content_words is a within-document mean of token frequencies in this extractor, not an external frequency rank. Richness, hapax and entropy share content-token counts. MTLD and Yule's K instead use all alphabetic words.
lexical_frequency_information.title: Lexical information around a frequency scaffold
lexical_frequency_information.interaction: Content richness and within-document mean frequency form a decreasing curved scaffold in both classes. Entropy, hapax, MTLD and Yule context occupy it differently in some genres: reviews show thin AI entropy strands, legal has a fork, and articles have a restricted AI segment. The scaffold itself is shared and count-constrained.
lexical_frequency_information.exceptions: Abstracts overlap substantially, and papers show entropy rising with richness in both classes rather than the decreasing primary-genre appearance. avg_freq_rank_content_words is not an external frequency rank. No independent cross-genre lexical mechanism is nominated here.

genres.email: AI occupies a restricted high-richness region while Human extends more broadly along the entropy/richness arrangement. The frequency/richness curve is shared. Extra lexical-variation shifts do not yet establish a necessary collective response.
genres.review: AI entropy follows near-constant strands across a broad richness range, while Human more often follows a falling entropy/richness arrangement. The decreasing within-document-frequency curve remains shared. Retain the local entropy strand as an extension of earlier lexical observations.
genres.legal: AI entropy has an upper fork and a lower high-richness band while Human is more continuous. Both share the decreasing frequency/richness scaffold. The branch pattern is local.
genres.abstracts: Richness/entropy clouds overlap substantially and AI occupies a shorter segment of the shared frequency curve. No distinct recurring response was established.
genres.articles: AI occupies a narrow high-richness segment with entropy spread, while Human extends more broadly along a falling arrangement. Frequency remains on the shared curve; MTLD/Yule context differs but its necessary role is unproved.
genres.papers: Entropy rises with richness in both classes, unlike the decreasing appearance of several primary genres. Within-document frequency still decreases with richness. Sparse papers are an explicit geometry variant, not support for a universal entropy slope.
